speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail? I also need to know if the fever, rhinorrhea, and headache started before or after the rash appeared.

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her face have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and is the rash on her body lacy or reticular in pattern? Has she been exposed to anyone with similar symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild prodromal symptoms, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth disease (Parvovirus B19 infection)
